title: The Boeing Company Executive Layoff Benefits Plan (As Amended and Restated Effective January 1, 2025)

nodes.title: Section 1. Purpose of the Plan
nodes.summary: The Boeing Company Executive Layoff Benefits Plan, Exhibit 10.13, was established in 1997 to provide layoff benefits to executives, amended and restated for events from 2017, and further amended and restated effective January 1, 2025. It is intended to be an ERISA welfare benefit severance pay plan, with payments exempt from Code Section 409A, and must be interpreted consistently with those purposes.

nodes.title: Section 2. Terms and Definitions
nodes.summary: Section 2 states that its definitions apply only to this Plan. It defines affiliates/subsidiaries by reference to federal tax-law controlled groups and service groups; base salary excludes bonuses, incentives, benefits, and perquisites; and identifies the Code, ERISA, Committee, Compensation Committee, Company, Employee, Incentive Plan, Plan, and calendar-year Plan Year. Equivalent Employment requires an offer before a layoff event with at least 90% of prior base salary and applicable incentive target, within 70 miles. Involuntary Layoff means position elimination; Layoff Benefit and Layoff Event are defined in other sections; Service follows PRO-100. Specified Employee status follows Code Section 409A, determined annually from the prior year’s final day for effect April 1, using up to 75 top-paid officers instead of 50 where permitted.

nodes.title: Section 3. Eligibility and Layoff Event.
nodes.summary: To qualify for a Layoff Benefit on the event date, an employee must be on U.S. executive payroll, have at least one year of service, and experience an involuntary layoff. A layoff is excluded if the employee joins or refuses eligible company or affiliate employment within 90 days; continues in or is offered equivalent employment following a business transfer, outsourcing, or operator/contract change; results from a disaster or national emergency, strike or similar disruption; or the employment ends for another reason, including voluntary or temporary layoff, assignment completion, resignation, dismissal, retirement, death, or leave of absence.

nodes.title: Section 4. Layoff Benefit.
nodes.summary: The Layoff Benefit equals one year’s pre-layoff base salary plus the applicable annual target incentive, adjusted for any payments under individual employment or severance agreements; incentive amounts subject to clawback are excluded, and Plan payments replace—not supplement—Incentive Plan awards. Salary and incentive portions have separate lump-sum payment deadlines, subject to Section 409A timing rules, including a six-month delay for certain specified employees. Payments are taxed through withholding, accrue no interest, are limited to one per employee, may be recovered if unpaid under the Plan, and may offset acknowledged debts. Payment requires a claims release; unpaid benefits do not pass after death. The Committee may forfeit benefits for up to five years after employment for specified criminal conduct, competition, employee solicitation, disparagement, or misuse of confidential information, with exceptions for protected communications and testimony. Forfeiture may be enforced or narrowed by a court, and incentive-related clawbacks may require reimbursement.

nodes.title: Section 5. Administration.
nodes.summary: The Committee is the Plan’s ERISA administrator and named fiduciary, with authority to interpret and administer the Plan, decide eligibility and benefit questions, and issue final, binding decisions within its authority. It must establish rules for benefit applications and other administrative matters, and procedures for claims and review of denials; review decisions are final subject to legal appeal rights. Members must exercise ordinary care and diligence, are protected from personal liability for specified acts or others’ misconduct, and are indemnified by the Company to the fullest extent allowed under its bylaws.

nodes.title: Section 6. General Provisions.
nodes.summary: The Committee may amend or terminate the Plan, including retroactive changes to meet legal requirements. The Plan is unfunded, with benefits paid from Company assets; benefits and benefit periods do not count as compensation or service and cannot be deferred into the 401(k) or another deferred arrangement. Benefits cannot be transferred or subjected to legal process. The Plan grants no right to continued or recalled employment. Special payment rules apply when an Employee cannot provide a valid receipt, and final payments discharge related claims. Federal law and, where applicable, Delaware law govern; invalid provisions are severed. Benefit lawsuits must be filed within 180 days after an appeal decision or appeal deadline. The Committee may modify provisions concerning Non-Exempt Amounts to comply with Code Section 409A.

summary: The Plan’s purpose, ERISA and tax treatment, definitions, and eligibility rules are set out, including qualifying involuntary layoffs and exclusions. Benefits are calculated from base salary and target incentive, subject to agreement offsets, payment and tax rules, release requirements, clawbacks, and post-employment forfeiture provisions. The Committee administers claims and decisions and has specified fiduciary protections. General provisions address amendment and termination, funding, employment rights, transfer restrictions, governing law, claim deadlines, and 409A compliance.

title: The Boeing Company 2003 Incentive Stock Plan

nodes.title: Section 1. Purpose of the Plan
nodes.summary: Exhibit 10.14 presents Boeing’s 2003 Incentive Stock Plan, amended and restated effective January 1, 2025. Its purpose is to attract, retain, and motivate employees and other specified service providers while aligning their interests with shareholders’ long-term interests. The plan was replaced by the 2023 plan after shareholder approval at the 2023 annual meeting and remains effective only for awards outstanding then.

nodes.title: Section 2. Definitions
nodes.summary: Defines the plan’s key terms, including cash-flow measures; company officers, committees, participants, awards, options, stock-based and cash awards; stock and fair market value; grant dates; performance goals and periods; related companies; and accounting, securities, tax, and plan references. It also defines disability, layoff, retirement, and termination of service, including who determines termination, transfers between wholly owned entities, and departures when an entity ceases to be related. The shareholder approval date and rules for substitute awards are specified.

nodes.title: Section 3. Administration
nodes.summary: The Plan is administered by the Compensation Committee, except nonemployee director awards, which are administered by the Governance & Public Policy Committee unless the Board decides otherwise. Committees generally require at least three independent, nonemployee directors; a member’s failure to qualify does not invalidate an otherwise valid award. The Board or Committee may delegate administration to other Board committees or, within prescribed limits and subject to legal restrictions, officers; officers cannot award themselves or Section 16 officers. The Committee selects eligible recipients and award types, sets share amounts and terms, approves agreements, determines settlement, cancellation, suspension and deferral, interprets and administers the Plan, establishes rules and agents, delegates ministerial tasks, makes specified Section 10D-related amendments, and takes other necessary actions. Its decisions bind all affected parties; a majority determines actions and meeting arrangements.

nodes.title: Section 4. Shares Subject to the Plan
nodes.summary: The Plan authorizes up to 80 million shares plus up to 7 million unused, unencumbered Old Plan shares. Shares may be newly issued or treasury stock; the Committee determines fractional-share treatment, and specified changes in stock designation or par value do not alter Common Stock status. Shares generally count only when issued and delivered; expired, forfeited, cancelled, cash-settled, or reacquired awards return to the pool, while specified tendered, withheld, cash-settled, excess SAR, and substitute-award shares do not count. The Committee may use awards to satisfy other compensation rights. Annual limits include 2 million shares per participant for options/SARs, performance or cash-award value equal to 1 million shares, $1 million in director award value, 4 million unrestricted or short-service-restricted shares, and 2 million incentive stock option shares, subject to stated adjustments and overall limits.

nodes.title: Section 5. Eligibility
nodes.summary:
Section 5. Eligibility
An Award may be granted to any employee, officer or director of the Company or a Related Company whom the Committee from time to time selects. An Award may also be granted to any consultant, agent, advisor or independent contractor who is a natural person and who provides bona fide services to the Company or any Related Company. The above are “eligible persons.”

nodes.title: Section 6. Awards
nodes.summary: The Committee may choose award types, grant them individually or alongside other awards, and document their terms in writing consistent with the Plan. It may allow payment deferrals under rules it sets, including additional awards or interest/dividend credits, provided deferrals comply with Section 409A. Participants may receive dividends or equivalents on awards, subject to Committee-set forms and restrictions; legacy awards follow Section 11. Option and stock appreciation right dividend rights cannot depend on exercise and must meet Section 409A requirements, while equivalents on performance-based awards are subject to the same vesting and forfeiture risks.

nodes.title: Section 7. Options
nodes.summary: The Committee may grant incentive or nonqualified stock options. Exercise prices must be at least 100% of grant-date fair market value, except for substitute awards, and repricing is prohibited without shareholder approval. Options may last up to ten years. The Committee sets vesting, exercise procedures, and post-termination terms; exercises require whole shares, required documentation, and full payment before issuance. Permitted payment methods include cash, wire, attested shares, broker-assisted sale or loan, or other approved consideration. Incentive options must comply with Code Section 422, are limited to eligible employees, and amounts exceeding the annual $100,000 (or applicable Code limit) are treated as nonqualified options. No incentive options may be granted more than ten years after the Plan’s February 2014 adoption.

nodes.title: Section 8. Stock Appreciation Rights
nodes.summary: The Committee may grant tandem or freestanding SARs, setting tandem grant prices equal to the related Option’s exercise price and freestanding prices at grant-date fair market value, except for Substitute Awards. The Committee sets exercise terms; freestanding SARs last no more than ten years, while tandem SARs cannot outlast their Options and require surrender of equivalent Option rights, covering only exercisable shares. Exercise payment equals the share-count times the excess of exercise-date fair market value over grant price, payable in cash, shares, a combination, or another approved form. Freestanding SARs’ post-termination exercise terms are set in their instruments and may be modified subject to Section 409A. Repricing actions require prior shareholder approval.

nodes.title: Section 9. Restricted Stock and Stock Units
nodes.summary: Sections 9–12 cover restricted stock and stock units, performance-based awards, other awards, and withholding. The Committee sets award terms and restrictions, which may be waived; satisfied restrictions make restricted shares transferable, while stock units are paid in cash, shares, or both. Performance shares and restricted awards pay in shares (or, at the Committee’s discretion, cash), while performance units pay cash (or may be converted to shares), subject to goals and possible adjustment. The Committee may also grant other cash- or stock-based incentives, including certain dividends. Participants must satisfy tax withholding and other obligations before shares issue, using cash, withheld or tendered shares, withheld cash, or mandatory share sales, subject to limits on share value withheld.

nodes.title: Performance Awards, Other Incentives, and Withholding
key_items: Section 10. Performance Shares, Performance Restricted Stock or Units, and Performance Units
Section 11. Other Stock or Cash-Based Awards
nodes.summary: The Committee may grant performance share and restricted stock/unit awards payable in shares, or performance units payable in cash, with outcomes subject to goals, specified terms, discretionary adjustments, and possible cash or share substitutions. It may also grant other cash- or stock-based incentives, including dividends and dividend equivalents on certain existing awards. Participants must satisfy tax withholding and other amounts owed before shares are issued, using cash, withheld cash or shares, tendered shares, or sale proceeds, subject to limits on share value withheld or sold.

summary: The amended and restated 2003 Boeing Incentive Stock Plan sets out its purpose, defined terms, administration, eligible participants, share pool and annual limits, and rules for granting and managing awards. It addresses options and SARs, restricted stock and units, performance and other cash- or stock-based incentives, dividends and deferrals, exercise and settlement, vesting and termination, withholding, and related legal and tax requirements. Replaced by the 2023 plan, it remains effective for awards outstanding when that plan was approved.

title: Section 13. Assignability
summary: Section 13 prohibits participants and beneficiaries from transferring, selling, pledging, encumbering, or otherwise disposing of awards or related rights. Exceptions allow transfer by will or intestate succession and, at the Committee’s discretion, designation of beneficiaries to receive payment after death. Awards are protected from legal seizure for debts and similar obligations, and during a participant’s lifetime may be exercised only by the participant or, upon legally established incapacity, a legal representative.

title: Section 14. Adjustments
summary: Section 14 preserves the Board’s and shareholders’ authority to undertake corporate actions, with no claims against Company-related parties arising from them. It requires equitable Award adjustments for specified distributions and corporate events to prevent dilution or enlargement of benefits, covering grant limits, outstanding Awards, and exercise or grant prices. For a Corporate Transaction, the Board may replace Awards with value-preserving substitutes, cancel options or stock appreciation rights for any positive transaction-price spread, and fairly adjust or settle other Awards; recipients’ affected Awards are canceled without consent, and unvested Awards do not automatically vest. The section defines Corporate Transactions through specified ownership, asset-sale, merger, or Board-composition changes, and defines transaction price as the highest related per-share price, with non-cash value determined in good faith under applicable law.

title: Section 15. Amendment and Termination
summary: The Board or Committee may amend, suspend, or terminate the Plan, subject to shareholder approval where required by law, exchange rules, or for material revisions—including weakening the anti-repricing rules or increasing available shares. The Plan ends ten years after shareholder approval unless ended earlier; no new Awards may then be granted, though existing Awards continue under their terms. Incentive Stock Options cannot be granted more than ten years after the Plan’s February 2014 adoption. Changes cannot materially harm participants’ existing Award rights or disqualify Incentive Stock Options without consent, except adjustments under Section 14.

title: Section 16. General
summary: Section 16 establishes award clawbacks under Board policy and for specified misconduct within two years of vesting or payment, subject to legal limits and protected communications; awards confer no entitlement, uniform treatment, or employment rights. Share issuance is conditioned on legal compliance, with no registration duty and authority for transfer restrictions or uncertificated shares. It provides indemnification for plan administrators, limits shareholder rights before share issuance, and addresses Exchange Act, ISO, and Section 409A compliance, including amendments and payment delays. The Committee may adapt awards for foreign laws; the plan is unfunded, successor obligations continue, invalid provisions are severable, and Delaware law governs unless otherwise specified.

title: The Boeing Company 2023 Incentive Stock Plan

nodes.title: Section 1. Purpose of the Plan
nodes.summary: The Boeing Company’s 2023 Incentive Stock Plan, as amended and restated effective January 1, 2025, aims to attract, retain, and motivate eligible persons while aligning them with shareholders’ long-term interests. Approved by shareholders at the 2023 annual meeting, it replaced the 2003 Plan, which remains in effect only for awards outstanding on the effective date.

nodes.title: Section 2. Definitions
nodes.summary: Defines the Plan’s key terms, including awards, company and governance roles, plans, eligibility, grant dates, fair market value, options, shares, and stock-based awards. It specifies performance goals and permitted adjustments; defines Related Companies with special rules for incentive options and Section 409A awards; and cross-references terms detailed elsewhere in the Plan. It also defines statutory terms, substitute awards, and tax obligations, and explains how Termination of Service is determined, including transfers among Related Companies and entities that cease to qualify.

nodes.title: Section 3. Administration
nodes.summary: The Plan is administered by the Compensation Committee, except nonemployee-director awards are administered by the Governance & Public Policy Committee unless the Board decides otherwise; committee members generally must meet NYSE independence and Rule 16b-3 standards, with nonqualification not invalidating otherwise valid awards. The Board or Committee may delegate administration or limited award-granting authority, subject to legal, exchange, and Section 16 restrictions. The Committee has broad authority to select recipients and awards, set terms, manage settlement and deferral, interpret and administer the Plan, waive or accelerate awards, correct documents, and take other necessary actions; its decisions are binding and generally discretionary. Repricing options or stock appreciation rights is prohibited without shareholder approval, except for specified adjustments.

nodes.title: Section 4. Shares Subject to the Plan
nodes.summary: Section 4 sets the Plan’s share pool: 12.9 million new shares, eligible unused and recycled 2003 Plan shares, and specified 2003 Plan tax-withholding shares. Shares may be new or treasury stock; the Committee handles fractional values, and certain changes to share designation or par value do not affect treatment as Shares. It defines when shares are counted, recycled, excluded, or reduced for reinvested dividends, and permits substitute compensation awards. Subject to adjustments, annual participant limits are 3 million shares for options/SARs and 1.5 million for other stock awards; most awards require one-year vesting, with exceptions. ISO awards are capped at 5 million shares, and annual nonemployee-director compensation is capped at $1 million ($2 million for a nonexecutive chair).

summary: The amended and restated 2023 Incentive Stock Plan, effective January 1, 2025, replaces the 2003 Plan for new awards and seeks to attract, retain, and motivate eligible people while aligning them with shareholders. It defines key plan, award, eligibility, performance, tax, and service-termination terms. It assigns administration to designated committees or authorized delegates, grants broad discretion over awards, and restricts repricing without shareholder approval. It establishes the share pool, counting and recycling rules, substitute awards, participant and director compensation limits, ISO caps, and general vesting requirements.

title: Section 5. Eligibility

Section 5. Eligibility
An Award may be granted to any employee, officer or director of the Company or a Related Company whom the Committee from time to time selects, or any consultant, agent, advisor or independent contractor who is a natural person and who provides bona fide services to the Company or any Related Company (collectively, “Eligible Persons”).

title: Section 6. Awards
summary: The Committee has sole discretion to choose award types, grant them singly or alongside other awards, and set award terms. Non-director awards require written Notices of Terms; nonemployee directors’ awards follow the Director Plan, with the Plan controlling any conflict. The Committee may permit payment deferrals under its procedures, including additional awards or interest/dividend-equivalent credits, through a designated deferred account, provided arrangements comply with or are exempt from Section 409A. It may also credit dividends or equivalents on awards, set restrictions and payment form, but not for Options or SARs; credits on unvested awards remain subject to forfeiture and are paid only when the award vests and is paid, and must meet Section 409A requirements.

title: Section 7. Options
summary: The Committee may grant incentive or nonqualified stock options. Exercise prices must generally be at least 100% of grant-date fair market value, and option terms may not exceed ten years. The Committee sets vesting and exercise terms; vested options are exercised for whole shares through prescribed procedures and full payment, with automatic net exercise on expiration in specified circumstances. Reload options are prohibited. Permitted payment methods include wire transfer, tendered shares, broker-assisted sale or loan, net exercise, or other approved consideration. Post-service exercise terms are set in the notice and must comply with Section 409A. Incentive options must satisfy Code Section 422, are limited to eligible employees, and excess annual first-exercisable value is treated as nonqualified; grants must occur within ten years of the plan’s February 2023 adoption.

title: Section 8. Stock Appreciation Rights
summary: The text covers SAR grants, pricing, terms, tandem exercise rules, automatic exercise at expiry under specified conditions, payout calculations and forms, no reload feature, and post-termination exercise terms. It describes grants and settlement of restricted stock and units, including forfeiture conditions, and performance-based awards tied to goals, with possible adjustments or cash settlement. The Committee may also grant other cash- or share-based awards. The withholding section requires satisfaction of tax and other obligations before settlement and permits several payment or share-withholding methods.

title: Section 12. Withholding

nodes.title: Section 12. Withholding (intro)
nodes.summary: The Company may require participants to pay applicable tax withholding and other amounts owed before receiving award payments; awards need not be issued or settled until these obligations are met. The Committee may require payment in cash, withholding from cash otherwise payable, withholding or surrendering shares, or mandatory sale of shares with proceeds remitted. Shares used for tax withholding may not exceed the participant’s maximum withholding rate, or a lower rate needed to avoid adverse financial-accounting treatment.

nodes.title: Section 13. Assignability
nodes.summary: Awards and related rights generally cannot be assigned, transferred, sold, exchanged, pledged, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of, or seized through legal process to satisfy debts or other obligations. Exceptions allow testamentary transfer or intestate succession, and Committee-approved beneficiary designations for payment after death. During a participant’s lifetime, only the participant—or a legal representative acting under a legal order due to physical or mental incapacity—may exercise awards.

nodes.title: Section 14. Adjustments
nodes.summary: Section 14 preserves the Board’s and shareholders’ authority to undertake corporate actions, without claims by participants or others arising from them. It requires equitable award and share-limit adjustments for specified distributions, capital changes, and other events to prevent dilution or enlargement of benefits. For Corporate Transactions, the Board may replace awards with value-preserving substitutes, cancel options or stock appreciation rights for any excess of transaction price over exercise price, and fairly adjust or settle other awards; affected awards are canceled upon substitute award or payment, without consent, and unvested awards do not automatically vest. The section defines Corporate Transactions (50% voting-power acquisition, substantially-all-assets sale, qualifying merger or consolidation, or Board-majority change, with an incumbent-director rule) and Corporate Transaction Price as the highest related per-share price, valuing noncash consideration in good faith under applicable law.

nodes.title: Section 15. Amendment and Termination
nodes.summary: The Board or Committee may amend, suspend, or terminate the Plan, subject to required shareholder approval; amendments requiring shareholder approval may be made only by the Board. NYSE-defined material revisions—including weakening the ban on repricing Options or SARs without approval or increasing available shares—must go to shareholders. The Plan ends ten years after its Effective Date unless ended earlier; no new Awards may then be granted, but existing Awards remain governed by their terms. Changes may not materially harm participants’ existing Award rights or disqualify Incentive Stock Options without consent, except for Section 14 adjustments.

nodes.title: Section 16. General
nodes.summary: Section 16 establishes award clawbacks for specified misconduct, subject to policy, law, timing, and protected-communication exceptions; denies any right to receive awards or continued employment; conditions share issuance on legal and exchange compliance and permits transfer restrictions and uncertificated shares; indemnifies plan administrators and officers; denies shareholder rights before share issuance; addresses Section 16, incentive-stock-option, and Section 409A compliance, including payment timing and amendments; permits foreign-law subplans and pricing methods; defines the plan as unfunded; binds successors; provides severability and Delaware governing law; and preserves participants’ rights to communicate with or assist government authorities.

nodes.title: 11. Clawback and Forfeiture Policy.

Where lawful, recovery may be deducted from future pay or awards. Compliance is a condition of the award, and the rules cover related companies. Legally protected communications to government agencies and sworn testimony are exempt.

title: Prohibition on Insider Trading

nodes.title: Purpose
nodes.summary: This policy explains the federal-law prohibition on insider trading and establishes enterprise-wide controls to promote and monitor compliance. It applies to all Boeing employees, contingent workers, consultants, contractors, agents, and Board members across all functions and business units. Violations may lead to individual criminal and civil penalties, including imprisonment and fines; penalties for Boeing and civil liability for controlling persons; and company sanctions, including dismissal, even if no law is violated.

nodes.title: Program
nodes.summary: Boeing’s insider-trading procedure bars Covered Persons aware of material nonpublic information (MNPI) from trading Boeing or related customer, supplier, negotiating, or transaction-company securities, tipping others, or recommending trades; these duties extend to informed family members and entities. After official disclosure, wait 48 hours, including several NYSE trading hours. Specified 401(k), savings-plan, and global stock-purchase-plan elections count as trades. A 30-day post-filing trading window is urged; derivatives and short sales are discouraged. Designated Insiders need pre-clearance for Boeing trades, generally only during windows, and clearance expires after two business days; they face additional bans on derivatives, short sales, margin, borrowing, hedging, pledging, and monetization. Their Rule 10b5-1 plans require advance written approval and compliance with law. Restrictions persist after covered status ends while MNPI remains nonpublic and material; questions should go to a Risk Area Focal or the Corporate Secretary.

nodes.title: Responsibilities for Securities Trading Compliance
nodes.summary: Covered Persons must follow this procedure and insider trading laws. Risk Area Focals answer business-unit or function questions and guide compliance with securities-trading requirements and responsibilities. The Corporate Secretary provides trading guidance, authorizes Designated Insiders to trade Boeing securities, and, with the Chief Legal Officer, approves their Rule 10b5-1 plans.

nodes.title: D. Chief Compliance Officer
nodes.summary: The Chief Compliance Officer investigates alleged insider trading and refers significant allegations to the Law Department under company policy. The text defines the Corporate Secretary, Designated Insiders (including certain former leaders for 90 days), Family Members, and entities a Covered Person controls or influences. It defines Material Information, lists examples spanning business, financial, personnel, securities, legal, cybersecurity, program, and regulatory developments, and advises treating uncertainty as material and avoiding trades. Material Nonpublic Information is material information not officially disclosed. Trading includes securities purchases, sales, gifts, and specified employee-plan transactions, with exceptions for certain automatic tax-withholding sales and bona fide gifts. Questions may be directed to Risk Area Focals or the Corporate Secretary.
